paragraphs.text: The University of Mississippi Medical Center in Jackson won AuntMinnie.com’s 2026 award for Best Radiologic Sciences Program. For Pontotoc County students considering a career taking X-rays, UMMC offers a bachelor’s degree. Closer to home, Itawamba Community College offers an associate degree in Tupelo.

ICC admits one class each fall. Students complete five semesters for an Associate of Applied Science and become eligible for the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists exam. The program requires prerequisites and an ACT score of at least 18. ICC lists a health science adviser at 662-620-5239 for questions about the program.

UMMC’s traditional bachelor’s program lasts 22 months. Applicants for fall 2027 need at least 60 hours of qualifying college credit, a cumulative GPA of 3.0 and an ACT superscore of at least 18. The university requires scores from all four ACT sections, including science. Application materials and the $25 fee are due Feb. 15.

UMMC reports that 95.6% of graduates of its traditional program passed their certification exam on the first attempt within six months of graduation. Its separate master’s program in magnetic resonance imaging also reported results this month. Every graduate passed the MRI credentialing exam on the first try for 10 straight years.
